text:
jess_support: Heads-up — multiple customers reporting p95->p99 latency regressions and intermittent auth timeouts (504) in us-west-2 since ~06:10 UTC. Affected routes: /v1/chat and /v1/generate. Errors spike aligns with increased hostfs write latency in logs.

maria_oncall: Thanks Jess. Any recent infra changes in usw2? kernel/driver/firmware?

jon_infra: We started a phased CUDA driver rollout (535.23) to a subset of hosts in us-west-2 at ~05:50. I'll paste the dmesg fragment from one affected host:

```
[05:53:12] nvme0: I/O 1024 queued, qdepth 128 -> latency spike
[05:53:12] nvme nvme0: reset controller due to timeout
[05:53:15] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3a:00.0: host reset triggered
```

kevin_sre: Observed kvcache eviction rate jump on prod-kv in the same time window. Evictions cause writebacks to hostfs which then show NVMe qdepth spikes. Looks like the driver rollout + eviction pressure is a bad mix.

jess_support: Customer repro (from ACME): run repeated chat streaming with ~64k context -> after ~200 concurrent sessions we see auth service returning 504 and generation requests timing out. Auth logs show upstream token-db timeouts around same timestamps.

maria_oncall: Mitigation suggestions: 1) route traffic away from nodes with 535 driver, 2) temporarily reduce concurrency (batching) for us-west-2, 3) enable model fallback to smaller variant for hosted customers to reduce KV pressure. Can infra do (1) quickly?

jon_infra: Yes — we can throttle route affinity. Plan: mark hosts with driver=535 as draining and shift new sessions. Also preparing rollback to previous driver build on a small pool for verification.

kevin_sre: Short repro steps for infra:
1) curl -X POST /v1/chat with streaming and 60k context payload in a tight loop
2) watch kvcache metrics: kvcache.evictions_per_minute, kvcache.writeback_bytes
3) monitor host NVMe qdepth and iostat -x for p95/p99

Command snippets:
```bash
# watch NVMe latency
iostat -x 1 10 | awk 'NR>6 {print $1,$14,$13}'
# kv cache evictions
kubectl logs -l app=kvcache -c metrics | grep evict
```

jess_support: I've drafted a short customer update to send after we confirm mitigations. Suggest message: "We're investigating increased latency in us-west-2; we've routed traffic to unaffected capacity and are rolling back a recent driver change as a precaution. More updates in 30m." Thoughts?

maria_oncall: Good. Add that we're offering a scoped SLA credit if they see continued impact. Also attach status page link. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy: started rollback -> driver-package:535.23 -> previous:534.88 on nodes [i-0a1b2c3d, i-0d4e5f6g] (rolling update)

jon_infra: I'm also raising NVMe queue depth tunables on affected hosts to reduce reset frequency (temporary). Command used:
```bash
echo 256 > /sys/block/nvme0/queue/nr_requests
```
Note: will monitor for side effects.

kevin_sre: If rollback reduces kvcache evictions and NVMe qdepth drops, that's a strong signal driver-related. If not, we'll pivot to auth upstream investigation (token-db). Collect these logs: nvme_qdepth, nvme_lat_p99, kvcache_evictions, authsvc_upstream_timeouts, dmesg.

jess_support: Notifying customers now. Template ready, sending to CSMs and affected account contacts.

maria_oncall: Quick operational checklist for post-incident:
- Save bisect artifacts (node metadata, kernel/driver versions)
- Capture heap/profile of authsvc if token-db timeouts persist
- Schedule 1-hour postmortem with infra/sre/support/eng-runtime

jon_infra: Rollback completing on first batch. Early signal: NVMe qdepth and hostfs write latency trending down on rolled-back nodes.

kevin_sre: Applying traffic-shift and concurrency prescale now (reduce to 60% for us-west-2 for 15m) -> expecting immediate p95 improvement.

deploy-bot: deploy: rollback batch 1 complete.

jess_support: Customer update sent. First replies: customers seeing partial improvement, some still report intermittent timeouts. Monitoring.

maria_oncall: Status check 30m after action: p95 back near baseline, p99 reduced by ~65% from peak. Auth timeouts dropped but not fully resolved — ongoing tracing on token-db path. Creating incident ticket for deeper triage and vendor follow-up on driver behavior.

kevin_sre: Agree — postmortem to include: driver rollout gating, kvcache eviction safety limits, and routing safeguards.

jess_support: Thanks team. I'll keep customers updated and escalate billing/SLA follow-up if needed.

maria_oncall: Closing immediate mitigation loop. Leaving incident open for postmortem docs and verification. :white_check_mark:
